**Finding: compliant (preferred level) — no redline proposed.**

The licence grant in Section 13 already satisfies every preferred element:

- **Affiliates and contractors** — § 13.1 grants the subscription rights directly to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf"; § 13.2 repeats Affiliate coverage and contractor support for paid-up material. No written-notice gate is needed, so the fallback is exceeded.
- **Paid-up perpetual and irrevocable** — § 13.2 grants a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence," and § 14.3 extends it to Vendor Technology required to use a Deliverable.
- **Subscription revocation limited to uncured material breach** — § 13.3 bars revocation or suspension except for a material uncured payment or use breach, after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity.
- **Successor transfer** — § 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor, keyed to § 24.1, which allows consent-free assignment to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or asset sale, with § 24.4 blocking Vendor repricing or termination on Customer change of control.

Context only (not flagged here): § 14.2 gives Customer a "revocable, non-transferable licence" in Deliverables, which contradicts §§ 13.2–13.3. That Deliverable ownership/licence term is addressed once under the IP rule to avoid double-flagging the same commercial bargain.
